newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - NYH distillates extend drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - NYH distillates extend drop.

text.p: New York Harbor (NYH) distillate differentials continued their downward spiral Tuesday morning, with prompt heating oil differentials weakening in the face of the stronger NYMEX prices.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), June heating oil futures were up 0.80 cents in early action, while June gasoline was up 0.11 cents.
++ Heating oil diffs eased a half cent from late Monday with offers of 2.25 cents over June futures and low sulfur diesel dipping 0.75 cent to about 2.25 cents over.
"It's May, so I'm not surprised," one East Coast player said, adding the market was fully expecting distillates to continue easing as warmer weather approaches.
"It's got a little further to go," the trader said, noting Tuesday's differential loss came on the heels of a half cent slippage seen Monday.
++ Gasoline diffs in NYH were stable with "M2" conventional unleaded offered at 2.0 cents under the June print and "A2" reformulated at 1.0 cent over.

++ Traders said differentials remained little changed across the board for products, with back-13th-cycle (prompt) heat offered at 2.10 cents under benchmark futures and "M1" (conventional) unleaded gasoline at 4.0 cents under.
++ Gasoline in Group Three eased early in the day, with unleaded pegged a half cent lower from Monday at 2.00 cents to 2.50 cents over NYMEX gasoline.
A prompt 2.25 cents deal over the screen was done in morning trade, and parcel for May 15 delivery was done at 0.50 cents over changed hands.
Offers for Group Three was talked a half cent lower at 5.50 cents over NYMEX heating oil.
